appSource.title: Source
appSource.description: This app deploys from a release — there's no repo to push to; updates ship as new versions.
appSource.cliManaged: This is the Openship control plane — it updates itself. Run "openship update" on the host to upgrade it; there's nothing to change here.

toast.saveFailed: Could not save the container release source.

switchToImage.title: Switch to a prebuilt image source
switchToImage.description: Saving replaces the current Git or local source for every environment. Existing deployments and rollback history remain available.

switchToGit.title: Switch to a Git source
switchToGit.description: Nothing changes until you link a repository. Linking one replaces the tracked image source for every environment.

entry.description: Deploy a versioned registry image directly, without cloning or building a repository.

summary.title: Tracked container image
summary.description: Deploys a published image directly. No repository is cloned and no build command runs.

editor.templateHint: Use {tag} to preserve the publisher's exact tag, or {version} for the normalized version.
editor.githubDescription: Follow the latest published release tag.
editor.urlDescription: Read a version endpoint or deploy a fixed version.
editor.versionUrlHint: HTTPS endpoint returning text or JSON with version/tag_name.
editor.pinnedHint: Overrides the discovered latest version; leave blank to track updates.
editor.appliesAll: Changes apply to every environment in this project.

appSettings.saveHint: Save to store these changes — they apply the next time the app is deployed.
appSettings.restartNote: Apply now to restart the app with the new settings, or they take effect on the next deploy.
appSettings.redeployNote: Applying these changes recreates the app — you may need to re-authenticate its dashboard or CLI afterwards.
appSettings.secretSet: Set — leave blank to keep the current value
appSettings.unmanaged: This app has no configurable settings yet.

appInstall.nameHint: How this app appears in Openship.
appInstall.customRequired: Enter your domain, or pick another option.
appInstall.installFailedBody: It stopped before everything was running. The technical details carry the full build log.
appInstall.installCancelledBody: The containers and images it had created were removed, and data volumes were kept — installing again reuses them. Anything already live was left alone.
appInstall.destinationHint: Pick the server or cloud this app runs on.
appInstall.hostFitTitle: This server is smaller than {app} needs
appInstall.hostFitMemory: Needs {needed} of RAM — this one has {available}
appInstall.hostFitHint: Install it on a bigger machine, or pick another destination.
appInstall.routePortDesc: Reachable at the host address and port — no domain or Cloud needed.
appInstall.routeFreeDesc: A free subdomain on {domain}, routed by Openship Cloud.
appInstall.routeFreeNeedsCloud: Connect Openship Cloud to use a free subdomain.
appInstall.routeCustomDesc: Point a domain you own at this app.
appInstall.routeDomainDesc: Reach it on a domain — a free subdomain or your own.
appInstall.tcpPublishDesc: Publish it on the host so external tools can connect.
appInstall.tcpInternalDesc: Only other services in this app can reach it.
appInstall.tcpFirewallNote: Open port {port} on your server firewall to connect from outside.
appInstall.desktopReachNote: On desktop you can open it on localhost — or forward the port from Servers → Ports for a remote server.

mail.title: Set up mail
mail.subtitle: Deploy webmail on your own domain, or connect an existing mailbox.
mail.chooseSelfDesc: Full SMTP/IMAP + webmail (iRedMail) on your server — we provision everything.
mail.chooseConnectDesc: Deploy just the webmail UI, pointed at any external SMTP/IMAP provider — Amazon SES, Oracle Cloud, Gmail, Fastmail, and more.
mail.sendOnlyNote: {provider} only sends mail — it holds no mailboxes. IMAP has to point at wherever your mail is actually stored.
mail.sendOnlyNoInbox: No inbox yet? Set up a mail server here, then relay sending through {provider} →
mail.imapOnOurServer: Mailboxes read from {host} — this instance's own mail server. Only sending goes through {provider}.
mail.relayNote: This instance already runs a mail server. If the mailboxes are on it, relay sending from its Delivery → Sending tab instead: IMAP stays local and only sending goes to {provider}, per domain or per address, and its own webmail keeps working.
mail.hostnameHint: The public URL people open to read their mail, e.g. mail.example.com.
mail.hostsRequired: Enter both the IMAP and SMTP host.

rename.title: Rename project
rename.description: Changes the display name. Nothing is redeployed.
rename.label: Project name
rename.identityNote: The project keeps the identity “{slug}” — its URL, container names and volumes don't change. To change the URL, edit the domain under Domains & Routes.

projectStatus.title: Project Status
projectStatus.description: Control whether the project is live or paused

migration.title: Migration
migration.description: Move this project to another server
migration.noOtherServers: Add a second server to move this project to one.
migration.cloudLater: Server to server. Moving to or from Openship Cloud isn't supported yet.
migration.confirmSubtitle: Nothing changes until you start the move.
migration.downtimeNote: The project is offline while its data copies across and the new server starts it. Stateful services are down for the whole transfer.
migration.dnsNote: DNS still points at the old server — move your records once the new one is serving.
migration.intentMoveHint: The project moves. Its containers and volumes are removed from the old server once you confirm.
migration.intentCopyHint: The original keeps running. A second project is created on the new server with a copy of the data.
migration.downtimeNoteCopy: The project is briefly offline while its data is copied — the volumes have to be still to copy cleanly. It starts again on the old server as soon as the copy finishes.
migration.copyNoDomainsNote: The copy starts with no domains — the originals stay with the project that's serving them.
migration.scopeHintSome: {count} service(s) — the rest stay only on the original.

cache.title: Docker Build Cache
cache.description: Unused build cache is automatically limited to 5 GB per server
cache.clearBuildDesc: Remove unused cache across this project's Docker server
cache.clearBuildConfirm: Clear all unused Docker build cache on this server? Other projects may rebuild dependencies on their next deployment.
cache.clearBuildEmpty: No unused build cache to clear

transfer.title: Transfer & Clone
transfer.description: Move or duplicate this project to a different environment

danger.title: Danger Zone
danger.body: Deleting this project will permanently remove all deployments, custom domains, environment variables, and analytics data.

routing.title: Routing
routing.description: How the edge reaches this app's upstream
routing.intro: Choose how the edge addresses this project's container.
routing.note: Loopback port is recommended: a private 127.0.0.1 host port, stable across restarts and never network-exposed. Container IP is advanced (zero-downtime swaps; needs the edge on the Docker bridge; not supported on Docker Desktop).

internalAlias.title: Internal hostname
internalAlias.description: Custom name other services use to reach this app privately
internalAlias.intro: Set an extra DNS name for this app on its private project network. It resolves alongside the default (the project slug) — other linked services can use either. Public access is unchanged; this never exposes a port.
internalAlias.label: Hostname alias
internalAlias.hint: Letters, digits and dashes only. Leave empty to use the project slug.

toast.invalid: Enter at least one letter or digit

routeRules.title: Route rules
routeRules.description: Rate-limit, ban, and allow/deny rules enforced at the edge — applied instantly, no redeploy.
routeRules.empty: No route rules yet. Add one below.

live.title: Backup activity
live.description: Real-time progress for the run you just kicked off. Survives page refresh.

destinations.title: Backup destinations
destinations.emptyHint: Connect an S3 bucket, an SFTP host, or a server you already use.

services.title: Backup policies
services.description: Choose what to back up, when to run it, and where to store it.
services.empty: This project has no services yet. Service-level backups appear here once you add some.
services.createPolicyHint: Create a backup policy for this service
services.projectHint: One policy for all services in this project.

recent.title: Recent backups
recent.description: Recent runs, their results, and restore options.
recent.emptyHint: Create a policy, then run your first backup here.

overview.description: Schedule backups and restore your project data.

webmail.title: Managed by openship
webmail.description: Webmail uses a fixed build and start pipeline — install, build, and run commands are not configurable. Redeploy from the mail overview to pick up upstream changes.

services.title: Per-service settings
services.descriptionTemplate: This project has {serviceLabel}. Build commands, framework, ports, and run commands live on each service row — view and edit them in the Services tab.

runtime.title: Runtime configuration
runtime.description: Read-only. Edit through the deploy wizard so each change ships as a new version.

storage.title: Persistent storage
storage.description: Paths kept when a new version replaces the old one. Everything else in the container is discarded on deploy.
storage.saved: Storage updated. It applies on the next deploy.
storage.hint: One per line. A bare path is relative to the app (storage), or give a full mount (name:/app/path, /host/path:/app/path).

objectStorage.title: Object storage
objectStorage.description: An S3 bucket for uploads — survives redeploys and works with more than one replica, unlike a local path.
objectStorage.connected: Bucket verified and connected. It applies on the next deploy.
objectStorage.empty: No bucket connected. Uploads stay on the container's disk.

env.title: Project environment (build + shared runtime)
env.description: Used for image builds and shared runtime input. Compose values and service runtime overrides take precedence at runtime. Secrets stay masked.

envVars.applyText: Saved. Restart to apply runtime changes. Rebuild and redeploy to apply values used when building an image.
envVars.title: Project environment (build + shared runtime)
envVars.description: Production project variables. Secrets stay masked; leave a saved secret blank to keep it. Service runtime values take precedence for the same key.

toast.noChanges: No changes to save — your saved values were kept.
toast.applying: Restarting the service with the new env — no rebuild.
toast.applyFailed: Couldn't apply the env to the running service

envVars.linkedBody: This value comes from the {app} connection. Manage it from that app — changes made here won't stick.

connectFirst.title: Connect GitHub first
connectFirst.description: Link your GitHub account to connect a repository to this project.

link.description: Connect a GitHub repository to enable webhook-triggered deployments.

picker.title: Select a repository
picker.description: Choose a repository to link to this project

appBanner.title: GitHub App not installed
appBanner.description: Install the Openship GitHub App on your account or organization to enable auto-deploy and webhook-triggered deployments for cloud projects.

webhookBanner.title: Enable auto-deploy
webhookBanner.description: Auto-deploy needs a direct webhook endpoint. Expose this Openship API on a public URL or configure a verified webhook domain for direct delivery.

source.title: Source Repository
source.description: Git integration, deployment triggers, and repository health

webhookEndpoint.title: Webhook Endpoint
webhookEndpoint.descriptionSet: GitHub delivers push events directly to this domain
webhookEndpoint.descriptionUnset: Choose a domain for direct webhook delivery

webhookCard.title: Webhook
webhookCard.descInactive: Webhook has not been configured or is not responding

rollbackStrategy.title: Rollback strategy
rollbackStrategy.descRebuild: Rebuilds the old commit, unless its image is still on the host.
rollbackStrategy.descInstant: Keeps rollback artifacts within the history limit. Older versions may need to be rebuilt.
rollbackStrategy.descRebuildFiles: Rebuilds the old commit, unless its files are still on the host.
rollbackStrategy.descInstantFiles: Keeps built files within the history limit. Older versions may need to be rebuilt.

rollbackHistory.title: Rollback history
rollbackHistory.retentionHint: Keep recent deployment artifacts for quick rollback.
rollbackHistory.retentionDescription: Maximum number of past releases to keep. Active and pinned releases are extra. Older artifacts are removed; deployment history stays available. Set to 0 to keep only active and pinned releases.
rollbackHistory.descSnapshot: Older versions are pruned to reclaim disk.
rollbackHistory.descGit: Recent images are retained either way, so a rollback can skip the build.
rollbackHistory.descGitFiles: Recent versions' files are retained either way, so a rollback can skip the build.

commits.title: Recent Commits
commits.subtitle: Latest commits on {branch}
commits.emptyDesc: Push to your repository and recent commit activity will appear here.

cloneToken.title: Clone Token Override
cloneToken.description: Project-scoped token used by the clone module before falling back to your global token or the GitHub App
cloneToken.explainer: Paste a GitHub PAT here to use ONLY for this project. Highest priority in the clone chain - overrides your settings-level token and the GitHub App.

toast.rollbackWindowOne: Keeping the last {count} version for rollback
toast.rollbackWindowOther: Keeping the last {count} versions for rollback
toast.appNotInstalled: GitHub App is not installed for this account

logs.noRuntimeDesc: This project has no running server process and no domain, so there is nothing to stream. Add a domain and its edge request logs will appear here.
logs.targetDescProject: Switch between the project runtime and service runtimes.
logs.selectService: Select a service to view its runtime logs.

resources.title: Machine Power
resources.description: CPU and memory limits for this project's containers.
resources.appliesOnNextDeploy: Limits are applied when the container is recreated — redeploy for a change to take effect.

customPanel.boundedBy: This machine has {cpu} vCPU and {memory}. Enter 0 for no limit.
customPanel.capacityUnknown: Could not read this machine's capacity, so no ceiling is enforced. Enter 0 for no limit.

toast.invalidValues: CPU and memory must be 0 or a positive number

sleep.title: Machine Mode
sleep.infoBefore: When there are requests, your container stays running. After inactivity, it sleeps to save costs. On the next request, it wakes up

deleteDialog.title: Delete Project
deleteDialog.bodyPrefix: Are you sure you want to delete
deleteDialog.bodySuffix: ? This action cannot be undone and will permanently delete all project data, deployments, and settings.

deletion.title: Delete project
deletion.wipeOn: Volumes will be permanently removed - database contents, caches, uploads, everything stored by these services will be gone.
deletion.wipeOff: Off: containers are removed but their named volumes stay on disk. Re-attach them later by name.
deletion.amberWipe: All deployments, domains, env vars, and persistent service data will be permanently removed.
deletion.amberNoWipe: All deployments, domains, env vars, and analytics will be permanently removed.
deletion.recordOnlyDesc: Keeps the app and its data running on your server — only the Openship record is removed. You can re-import it later.
deletion.recordOnlyReversible: Reversible — the app stays on your server.
deletion.recordOnlyNote: Nothing on the server is touched — the app keeps running with its data. Only Openship's record is removed, and it can be re-imported later.
deletion.linkedTitleOne: {count} project is connected to this app
deletion.linkedTitleOther: {count} projects are connected to this app
deletion.linkedNote: They keep running with their data untouched — they only lose this connection. Redeploy them to pick that up.
deletion.linkedNoteRecordOnly: They keep running, but the link goes with the record — re-importing this app later won't restore it.

routing.title: Routing
routing.description: Rewrites, redirects & headers. Applied on save — no rebuild.

toast.title: Routing
toast.updated: Routing updated — applied to the live deployment.

add.title: Add domain
add.description: Add a route: pick a free or custom domain and the port it maps to.
add.servesPathHint: Requests to this domain are served from this path in your build output.
add.servesPathRedeploy: New paths take effect on your next deploy.
add.externalIngressDesc: TLS terminates at your reverse proxy (Cloudflare Tunnel, Nginx Proxy Manager, or a load balancer). The domain need not point at this server, and Openship won't issue a certificate.
add.dnsChallengeDesc: Verify through a DNS provider or a temporary TXT record. Useful when port 80 is unavailable.
add.dnsChallengeWildcardDesc: Required for wildcard HTTPS. Use a connected DNS provider, or add a temporary TXT record during HTTPS setup.
add.noWww: That domain is already on this project.

dns.title: DNS Records
dns.descPreview: Add these records at your DNS provider, then click Add domain to attach it
dns.descApply: Apply these records at your DNS provider, then wait for propagation
dns.infoPreview: Add these records first — they don't change after adding, so propagation starts now. Then press Add domain to attach it, and finally Verify once DNS resolves.
dns.infoApply: DNS changes can take up to 48 hours to propagate globally. Once the records resolve, click Verify below — we'll check DNS, mark the domain active, and provision SSL in the background.

records.hint: Add these at your DNS provider, then click Verify.
records.none: No records to add for this domain.
records.failed: Couldn't load the DNS records for this domain.

verifyMissing.both: Neither the CNAME nor the TXT record is resolving yet — add the records below, wait for DNS to propagate, then Verify.
verifyMissing.cname: The CNAME record isn't resolving yet — add it below, wait for DNS to propagate, then Verify.
verifyMissing.txt: The TXT verification record isn't resolving yet — add it below, wait for DNS to propagate, then Verify.

portHint.body: Nothing responded on port {port} — requests may 502 until the app listens there.
portHint.bodyService: Service "{service}": nothing responded on port {port} — requests may 502 until it listens there.

outputHint.body: No build output found at {path} — check your Output Directory and redeploy.
outputHint.noIndex: Output exists at {path} but there is no index file — requests will 404. Check your Output Directory.
outputHint.notServed: The edge answered HTTP {status} for {path} — this path is not serving. Check your Output Directory and the route.

edit.title: Edit domains
edit.descServer: Edit which internal port each domain should route to.
edit.descStatic: Edit which static path each domain should serve.

addRoute.emptySuffix: to point a domain at a service's port.

editRoute.title: Edit route
editRoute.disabledWarning: Service is disabled - routes are inactive until the service is re-enabled.

certUpload.title: Upload certificate
certUpload.desc: Serve TLS from your own certificate (bring-your-own or Cloudflare Origin CA) instead of Let's Encrypt. Use this when an upstream proxy fronts this domain and the origin still needs a real cert (Cloudflare Full-strict). Certbot is disabled for this domain once a certificate is uploaded — renew by uploading a new one.

toast.enterPort: Enter the port this domain should route to (1–65535).
toast.addedCustom: {label} added — apply the DNS records, then Verify.
toast.verifiedSuccess: {hostname} verified — SSL is provisioning in the background.
toast.sslNoCert: No valid certificate found for {hostname} yet. If you just deployed, give Let's Encrypt a moment, then recheck.
toast.completeEndpoints: Complete every domain and mapped port before saving
toast.publishing: Publishing — deploying to install the edge and apply your domain…
toast.publishFailed: Domain saved, but the deploy didn't start — redeploy to publish it.
toast.enterPortShort: Enter the port this domain should route to.
toast.noServicePort: No service publishes port {port}. Add that port to a service first.

diagnosis.title: Domain details
diagnosis.noneYet: No check has run yet, so there's no result to show. Add the DNS records shown for this domain, then run Verify.
diagnosis.scheduleHint: Checks run while this instance is online. Queued work can delay the start.
diagnosis.automaticDisabled: Automatic domain checks are disabled. Retry manually or enable them in Jobs.
diagnosis.scheduleUnavailable: The automatic check schedule is unavailable. You can retry manually.

reasons.verification: Domain verification has not completed. Check the DNS records before retrying.
reasons.certificate: HTTPS needs checking on the serving server. Retrying checks for an existing certificate before requesting one.
reasons.deployment: This route is waiting for a deployment. Deploy the project to apply it.
reasons.disabled: This project or service is disabled. Enable it before checking the route.
reasons.removing: This domain is being removed. No verification is scheduled.
reasons.manual_certificate: This domain uses an uploaded certificate. Upload a valid replacement, then recheck it. Openship does not renew it automatically.
reasons.managed_certificate: TLS is managed by your external proxy or Openship Cloud. Check that provider’s configuration.
reasons.route_missing: This configured route has not been applied. Retry routing to apply it. No automatic routing retry is scheduled.
reasons.manual_dns: This certificate uses manual TXT verification. Open HTTPS setup to confirm a new TXT record, or choose a connected DNS provider for automatic renewal.

wildcard.title: DNS-verified HTTPS
wildcard.scope: A wildcard covers one subdomain level. Add the base domain separately if it should serve this app too.
wildcard.notice: Wildcard HTTPS requires DNS verification. After saving, connect a DNS provider or add the TXT record from HTTPS setup.
wildcard.automaticHint: Connect Cloudflare in Settings → DNS to create certificate challenges and renew HTTPS automatically.
wildcard.manualHint: Add a temporary TXT record at your DNS provider. Each renewal needs a new TXT record; Openship will show when renewal is due.
wildcard.routing: 1. Point the domain at this server
wildcard.loadFailed: Could not load certificate setup. Retry to see its current state.
wildcard.recordsFailed: Could not load the routing DNS records. Your saved certificate challenge is still available.
wildcard.txtHint: Add this exact TXT value. Keep other TXT values at the same name. If your provider adds the zone name, enter only the relative part.
wildcard.cleanup: You may remove this attempt’s TXT value. Keep all other TXT records.

serviceEnvironment.title: Service runtime environment
serviceEnvironment.description: These variables apply only to this service and override matching Compose or shared project values. Use Apply environment changes to activate saved values.
serviceEnvironment.overrides: These keys take precedence over project values for this service: {keys}.
serviceEnvironment.buildArguments: Build arguments are configured in the Compose file or source configuration and require a rebuild.
serviceEnvironment.loadFailed: Could not load project variable names to check overrides.
